nodes.name: Cation Exchange Ru/NC
nodes.procedure: The Ru-based species dispersed on NC substrate was facilely synthesized by a cation exchange reaction under room temperature. Due to the weak acidity of RuCl₃ aqueous solution, H⁺ would attack the alkaline Na⁺ ions between CoO₂ slabs in NaCoO₂. The smaller radius of Ru³⁺ ion (0.82 Å) than that of Na⁺ (1.02 Å) allows easy access for Ru ions into the interlayer space of NaCoO₂. As a result, the Ru species would be deposited on the surface of CoO₂ slabs with the layered NaCoO₂ exfoliated simultaneously.

nodes.characterization_summary: Diffraction peaks of Ru/NC indexed to hexagonal NaCoO₂ phase with reduced intensity and shift to lower angles indicating enlarged interlayer spacing; broad peak at ~18° from amorphous Ru hydroxide.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Corresponding XRD patterns of the NC and Ru/NC samples were displayed in Figure 1a. After Ru treatment, the diffraction peaks of the Ru/NC catalyst were still indexed well with the hexagonal NaCoO₂ phase ... The broad peak at about 18° should be assigned to the amorphous Ru hydroxide deposited on the NC surface.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru/NC shows sheetlike exfoliated structure in cross-sectional view; NC shows agglomeration of large particles from high-temperature calcination.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As expected, the NC sample displayed agglomeration of large particles resulting from the high-temperature calcination (Figure S1, Supporting Information). The Ru treatment significantly changed its morphology. As observed in Figure S2 (Supporting Information), the sheetlike structure in the cross-sectional view of the Ru/NC sample indicated the successful exfoliation of the bulk NC.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru/NC shows disordered Ru hydroxide clusters (~1 nm, blue ellipses) monodispersed with neighboring Ru single atoms (red circles); uniform Ru distribution confirmed by elemental mapping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Numerous clusters with an average size of ≈1 nm were found monodispersed on the substrate (Figure 1b). The HAADF-STEM image of the Ru/NC (Figure 1d) showed that the disordered Ru hydroxide clusters (highlighted by blue ellipses) existed with neighboring Ru single atoms (highlighted by red circles), and the elemental mapping displayed in Figure 1e demonstrated the uniform distribution of Ru across the region selected.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru/NC substrate shows lattice spacing of 0.528 nm for (002) plane of NaCoO₂, larger than pristine NC (0.514 nm).
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) image of the substrate in Figure 1c showed continuous lattice spacing of 0.528 nm corresponding to the (002) plane of NaCoO₂. The larger lattice distance of NC substrate in Ru/NC than that of the pristine NC (0.514 nm, Figure S3).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru content in Ru/NC is ≈11.2 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ru content was ≈11.2 wt% as determined by the inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) measurement (Table S1, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: Dominant peak at 1-2 Å (Ru-O); broad shell at ≈3 Å from Ru-O-Co (single atoms) and Ru-O-Ru (clusters); excludes metallic Ru and crystalline RuO₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As observed from the corresponding Ru K-edge Fourier-transformed extended X-ray absorption fine structure (FT-EXAFS) spectrum of the Ru/NC (Figure 1f), the dominant peak at 1-2 Å was assigned to the Ru-O contribution. The broad coordinated shell at ≈3 Å consisted of Ru-O-Co and Ru-O-Ru contributions.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co-O (1-2 Å) and Co-Co (2-3 Å) contributions; multiple scattering Co-M peaks shifted to larger distance confirming enlarged layer spacing.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1g displayed the FT-EXAFS spectra of Co K-edge for the NC and Ru/NC samples. The scattering peaks at 1-2 and 2-3 Å were attributed to Co-O and Co-Co contributions, respectively ... the multiple scattering Co-M peaks of the Ru/NC all shifted to a larger distance than those of pristine NC.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru/NC: type-IV isotherm with H₃ hysteresis (rich mesopores), 31.12 m²/g, 0.11 cm³/g; NC: type-III non-porous, 3.45 m²/g, 0.008 cm³/g.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the nitrogen adsorption-desorption curves (Figure S5a,b, Supporting Information) of the bulk NC demonstrated a type-III isotherm without hysteresis loops ... the type-IV isotherm with H₃ hysteresis loops from the Ru/NC materials ... the Ru/NC sample possessed a much higher specific area of 31.12 m² g⁻¹ and a larger total pore volume of 0.11 cm³ g⁻¹ than those of the pristine NC (3.45 m² g⁻¹ and 0.008 cm³ g⁻¹).

nodes.characterization_summary: As-prepared Ru/NC average oxidation state +3.7; reduces to ≈+2.0 under HER potentials.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As plotted in Figure 3b, the Ru of the as-prepared Ru/NC was characteristic of an average valence of +3.7, whereas the oxidation state decreased to ≈+2.0 under HER potentials.

nodes.characterization_summary: Under HER: decreased Ru-O intensity/lengthened bond (reduced valence); Ru-O-Ru fades, Ru-Ru emerges (metallic clusters form); Ru single atoms maintained.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Upon applying HER potentials, the decreased peak intensity of Ru-O contribution and the enlarged Ru-O bond length corresponded to the reduced Ru valence state. More importantly, the peak that corresponded to Ru-O-Ru contributions in the Ru hydroxide clusters gradually faded, and simultaneously, a new scattering path that attributed to the Ru-Ru path in metallic Ru emerged.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru/NC has largest Cdl nearly 13× NC and 1.6× Pt/C, indicating significantly enlarged ECSA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ru/NC catalyst had the largest Cdl value that was nearly 13 and 1.6 times that of the original NC and commercial Pt/C, respectively (Figure 2d), demonstrating the significantly enlarged ECSA after Ru treatment.
